title: solver: derive contact reports from overlapping face support
body:
Contact pressure at a corner included uncontacted side faces in its reporting normal, understating pressure and normal force although the physical contact force and motion were correct. Closes #203.

The report now uses overlapping face-pair normals weighted by nodal mortar support. Small sliding keeps the reference pair normal; finite sliding follows the current overlap. Pressure, the scalar normal-force sum and reported shear share that direction. Physical force assembly, tangent, multipliers, gaps, the friction return map, active sets and convergence rules retain their existing definitions. Missing or cancelling support has no reporting direction and produces zero normal component instead of a manufactured direction or NaN.

The existing independent cube regression checks pressure = normal force / area even when all six secondary faces are selected. Plane-strain and one-layer solid C-ring regressions compare corresponding pressures and normal force, alongside the existing thread-count checks.

## Why the Hertz normal force moves farther from the load

`normal_force = Σ(-f_A · n_A)` adds **local** normal components. `force = Σ f_A` is the vector resultant. On a curved contact the scalar sum need not equal the resultant's vertical component. The old report used deformed full-face area vectors; the corrected small-sliding report uses the reference-pair normals used by the unchanged constraint. The old scalar happened to be closer to the vertical Hertz load.

A simple estimate predicts the difference: Hertz's `p(x) = p₀ sqrt(1-x²/b²)` has pressure-weighted `<x²> = b²/4`; circular normals therefore lose about `b²/(8R²)` of their vertical component. For `b = 0.5 mm`, `R = 10 mm`, that is **0.03125%**. This explains the scale; it does not replace the Hertz reference or change its tolerance.

Current Linux CPU traces from the original two oracle recipes:

| Case | Applied vertical load (N) | Resultant `force.y` (N) | Ground springs (N) | Old frozen scalar (N) | Corrected scalar (N) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `nl-hertz-cylinder` | 1132.785812592473 | 1132.770506982133 | 0.015305610423 | 1133.036636011328 | 1133.119329027206 |
| `nl-hertz-cylinder-plane-strain` | 1132.785812592473 | 1132.778159744225 | 0.007652848299 | 1133.044292624235 | 1133.126986729440 |

The ground-spring entries were calculated independently as the original spring stiffness times the summed top-node displacement. Resultant + springs balances applied load to **8.3e-11 N / 5.1e-11 N**; each resultant also matches its foundation reaction to about 3e-11 N. The 3D scalar exceeds its vertical resultant by 0.348822 N (0.030793%), consistent with the curvature estimate. Its 0.082693 N increase over the old scalar is a reporting projection change. The apparent error against the unchanged 1132.785813 N Hertz load rises from 0.02214% to 0.02944%, comfortably inside the existing 0.2% tolerance. The 2D scalar rises by 0.082694 N, to 0.03012% from that same reference.

The two Hertz READMEs and API docs explain this distinction. Only the eight intended report entries are refrozen below, using the oracle's existing band formula. Physical reference values, acceptance tolerances, all other fixtures, and the already matching depth-stress/zero-pressure entries stay unchanged.

## Validation

Current tested source: `eaf2cf45693eade2d34255488521e35d89e59cad`, rebased on develop `e8ee48d0`.

- `cargo check -p fieldcraft-solver` passed.
- `cargo test -p fieldcraft-solver`: **147 passed, 0 failed, 7 existing heavy tests ignored**; no doc examples.
- `cargo fmt --all`, scoped all-target clippy with warnings denied, manual simplification review and `git diff --check` passed.
- The narrow oracle first reproduced exactly eight moved reporting entries with all twelve physical-reference checks passing. Only `nl-hertz-cylinder` and `nl-hertz-cylinder-plane-strain` were blessed. The original depth-stress fixture entries were retained rather than rewriting insignificant 1e-10 platform round-off.
- Full default oracle **passed (exit 0)**: 82 normal cases executed, the existing nightly-only case checked by fixture, and all frozen quantities matched after the deliberate two-case blessing. Nine existing known-failure quantities and nine pending cases remain explicit. `docs/oracle.md` was regenerated; only six displayed Hertz rows change (the two tiny peak-pressure moves round to the same display values). There are no moved fixtures or error rows.

The oracle used the exact `fieldcraft-testkit` generator through `cargo run -p fieldcraft-testkit --bin oracle -- ...`, with the existing optimized development cache and four CPU threads. This was a CPU numerical run, not a release-profile build or a GPU test. No full local workspace gate, CI watching, new dependency, command, physical solver formulation or roadmap edit.

It shows the original two-cube setup with all six secondary faces, static compression, pressure contours and a real node-9 viewport probe near 9.992 MPa. Deformation scales and static-equilibrium interpretation are explicit. Its caption says the eight Hertz reports awaited fixture review at capture time; the current CPU work above resolves that review request. This is not a new hardware run of the rebased source.

The original native presented-frame and full-result/assembly-invariance audits remain evidence for that original capture and source. No fresh native or GPU numerical validation was possible in this environment. The recording and stills remain outside feature history. The original one-run recipe and explanation were removed from `docs/recipes/` and are reproduced below for review.

## Scope

This changes implicit contact output decomposition, not its friction law, contact discretisation or convergence behavior. It adds no quadratic contact faces or sliding semantics. Zero/cancelling support yields no normal direction; a finite force remains in reported shear where that field exists. A small-sliding curved normal sum remains distinct from a fixed-direction equilibrium load, as documented above.

## Reproduction of the original demonstration

# Contact reports at a surface corner

Run the original command recipe below in a fresh model:

```sh
cargo run -p fieldcraft-cli -- run /tmp/contact-corner-reports.json
```

The same array can be passed as `commands` to the desktop control channel's `engine.script`.
The recipe sets mm, N and MPa display units. Two touching 10 mm cubes each have one hex8
element, E = 1000 MPa and Poisson ratio zero. Every lower-cube node is fixed, the upper cube's
lateral translations are held, and its top is displaced down by 0.1 mm in one small-sliding
nonlinear static step. This is a static equilibrium, not a physical transient. Deformation is
displayed at 50 times its actual magnitude.

The main surface is the lower cube's top. The secondary surface deliberately includes **all six
faces** of the upper cube. Only its bottom overlaps the main surface. Its four bottom nodes
should each report pressure about 10 MPa and the upper nodes zero; the integrated normal force
is about 1000 N. The small remaining penetration follows the unchanged augmented-contact
convergence criterion. The actual pressure equals the actual normal force divided by the
100 mm² interface area, independently of that stopping gap.

The reporting direction is the unit sum of overlapping face-pair normals weighted by their
nodal mortar support (the integral of the secondary shape function over that overlap).
Uncontacted side and top faces contribute no support and cannot tilt this direction. Small
sliding uses the fixed reference pair's normal; finite sliding uses the current overlap's
projection normal. At a node whose support vectors exactly cancel, there is no reporting
direction: its reported normal component is zero, and any force remains in the shear component
when frictional shear is reported. No arbitrary fallback direction is chosen.

This correction changes the decomposition reported as pressure, normal force and frictional
shear. It leaves the assembled contact force, tangent, multiplier, gap, friction return map and
convergence controls unchanged. `crates/solver/tests/contact.rs` checks this independent flat
interface identity and compares the original closing C-ring's nodal pressure and normal force
between plane strain and a one-layer 3D model. Both rings need the support-based reporting
direction: the 2D surface also turns a corner at its contacting end, while the 3D surface has
additional uncontacted Z faces. Neither model's old report is a reference solution.

Save this original recipe as `/tmp/contact-corner-reports.json`:

comments.author: jyviko
comments.body:
Maintainer review and fixes. The branch is rebased onto develop, after #750 (quadratic mortar contact), and is still one commit. The fixes are folded into it.

**Findings (2026-10-28) and what changed**

1. **The friction law used a different normal from the report.** Fixed: the support-weighted normal is now the node normal, and both the law and the report use it. The separate `report_normal` field is gone. `State::normal` is Σ ∫ Φ_A n over the node's overlaps, normalised. Small sliding uses the reference pairs' normals; finite sliding uses the current projection normals. The value is zero where nothing overlaps or the overlaps cancel. The friction return map projects the committed traction on this normal's tangent plane, so the reported pressure, the reported shear and the cone the law enforces share one normal. The old normal summed every secondary face's area vector and tilted a cube's corners by about 55°. That code (`area_of` per face in `evaluate`) is removed. The friction slip operator was already per pair (fixed normal in small sliding, the current one in finite sliding), so the new normal is consistent with it. New regression `uncontacted_sides_do_not_tilt_the_friction_plane` has the upper block's six faces on the secondary surface. Its slipping bottom must carry μN, and every closed node must slip with reported |q| = μp within 0.5 %. It runs in small and finite sliding. On develop the same model reports |q|/(μp) of up to 25.8 at the corners; with this change every node is between 0.997 and 1.0004.
2. **One projection normal per pair (quadratic faces, #750).** Fixed: `Found` now carries ∫ Φ_a n per node, accumulated sample by sample. Each facet of a quadratic pair counts with its own normal, and the pair's last-sample normal is no longer used. Small-sliding pairs take the reference pair's normal, the mean normal for quadratic ones, scaled by the support. `uncontacted_corner_faces_do_not_tilt_reported_pressure` now runs hex8 and hex20 secondaries in both small and finite sliding.

**Rebase onto #750.** The rebase kept #750's `FACE_NODES` arrays, `integrate_pair` and `in_multiplier_basis`, and the new normal projects the multiplier-basis nodal forces. The gap and support sums keep their original operation order, so the assembled frictionless problem is unchanged and only the report moves.

**Separate finding, filed as #775.** A node's gap normalisation A_A counts uncontacted secondary faces. A hex20 cube with its sides on the secondary surface closes its bottom corners and mid-side nodes to slightly different gaps: about 1 % apart in pressure, against round-off with only the bottom face. The total force is right. This behaviour predates the PR and comes from the constraint, not the report. The hex20 check in the corner test therefore allows 3 % and cites #775.

The test module is renamed `contact/normal_tests.rs`, since it now covers the node normal and not only the report.

**Oracle.** Local run, CPU, macOS arm64; full default run, blessed only where listed:
- `nl-cattaneo-mindlin-cylinder` moves towards the closed form, because the friction law now uses the reference normal in small sliding. q(0)/p(0) goes from 3.13 % to 2.52 % off at Q = 0.5 μP and from 2.91 % to 2.29 % at 0.75 μP. p₀ moves from 0.124 % to 0.138 %, and the slip fractions are unchanged. The README is updated: its refinement table predates the change and is marked as such, its h = 0.025 values are given, and its paragraph on the report frame describes the new behaviour.
- `nl-hertz-cylinder-hex20` and `-tet10` (new with #750): normal_force moves from 0.024 % to 0.030 % off and from 0.023 % to 0.029 % off. This is the same reporting shift as the linear Hertz cases, explained in the PR description.
- `nl-friction-sliding-blocks/kinetic`: 4e-9 relative.
- The eight linear Hertz values the PR froze match unchanged.

`docs/oracle.md` is regenerated. Local `cargo test -p fieldcraft-solver` and clippy pass.

reviews.author: jyviko
reviews.body:
Thank you, a report-only change is nice and contained, and the friction law still uses `State::normal`. Before we refreeze the eight nl-hertz-cylinder values, I'd like to understand one move:

- `pressure_x0296` moves slightly toward theory (2257.84 → 2258.08, against 2325.07). 👍
- `normal_force` moves **away** from the applied load: 1133.04 → 1133.12 against 1132.79, so the error grows from 2.2e-4 to 2.9e-4. Can you explain why the new normals do that?

If the explanation holds, please refreeze the fixtures in the same commit. Also please move `docs/recipes/` into the PR description. One-run evidence lives in the PR, not the repo.

reviews.author: jyviko
reviews.body:
Reviewed. The Hertz refreezes are explained: normal_force moves from 0.022 % to 0.029 % off the reference, within the 0.2 % tolerance.

1. **Only the report changes, not the friction law.** The friction return map still projects with `state.normal`, which is built from every secondary face's deformed area vector, uncontacted sides included (`contact.rs` ~883-890, used ~1097-1107). At a cube's corner nodes the law's normal is tilted about 55°, and the PR's own test locks that in (`report_tests.rs:57`, `assert_ne!(state.normal, report_normal, …)`). The reported shear and the law now use different normals, so a node's reported shear/pressure can break the friction cone the law enforces. Please use the support-weighted normal in the law too, or, if that's a larger change, open an issue for it and reference it here. It's also the likely cause of #753's first-order slip-zone asymmetry.
2. `contact.rs:746,788` assume one projection normal per pair, which doesn't hold for quadratic faces (#750). Whichever lands second weights the normal per facet.
